notes: Primary constructor of this RuntimeException subclass. `aThrowable4595` is the wrapped original exception (never actually chained via Kotlin's `cause` mechanism, just stored as a plain field and accessible via the `@JvmField` for direct access from Java-derived call patterns); `aString4594` is a free-form diagnostic message built by callers as a fake 'method-call signature dump' (see method2929 notes) describing the arguments of the method that failed. Both fields are only ever touched via the companion factory method2929, never constructed directly anywhere else in the repo.

Companion/static factory used at the top of literally every `catch (runtimeexception: RuntimeException)` block across the entire codebase (100+ call sites in AbstractModel.kt, ByteBuffer.kt, Js5Archive.kt, Client.kt, CompositeNpcModelBuilder.kt, etc.), always as `throw TextureLoadException.method2929(runtimeexception, \<caller>.<method>(<args...>)\")`. Behavior: increments the companion call counter anInt6789; optionally prints the original stack trace when the `trace` companion flag is true (currently hardcoded false
column7: so dead in shipped builds); then if the incoming throwable is *already* a TextureLoadException
column8: it mutates that same instance's message by appending ` <string>` (building up a call-chain breadcrumb trail as the exception re-propagates up through nested catch blocks) and returns it unchanged in identity; otherwise it wraps the throwable in a brand-new TextureLoadException with the given message. Net effect: a single unified 'wrap on first throw
column9: append breadcrumbs on every re-throw up the stack' exception-context builder
column10: which is why the constructed message strings look like fake method-call signatures (`\"ka.AC(...)\"`
column11: `\"cea.JB(...)\"` etc.) -- these are the obfuscated call site's original class/method name plus a best-effort dump of its arguments
